title: Wildlife Tourism in Odisha: Similipal, Bhitarkanika and Chilika
seoTitle: Wildlife Tourism in Odisha: Similipal & Bhitarkanika | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Plan a wildlife trip in Odisha: Similipal's tigers and waterfalls, Bhitarkanika's crocodiles, Chilika's dolphins and birds, Satkosia and olive ridley nesting.
description: A guide to wildlife tourism in Odisha: Similipal Tiger Reserve with its waterfalls and melanistic tigers, Bhitarkanika's saltwater crocodiles and mangroves, Chilika lake's Irrawaddy dolphins and winter birds at Mangalajodi and Nalabana, Satkosia's Mahanadi gorge, olive ridley turtle nesting at Gahirmatha and Rushikulya, seasons and closures.
dek: Odisha combines tiger forests, mangroves, Asia's largest brackish lagoon and some of the world's biggest sea-turtle nesting beaches.

hero.alt: A saltwater crocodile basking on a mud bank in Bhitarkanika National Park

intro: Odisha has two tiger reserves, Similipal and Satkosia, along with Bhitarkanika's mangroves, the Chilika lagoon and a long coastline where olive ridley turtles nest in huge numbers. Similipal was one of India's original nine Project Tiger reserves in 1973.

Much of Odisha's wildlife is seen by boat: saltwater crocodiles in Bhitarkanika's creeks, Irrawaddy dolphins on Chilika, and gharials in the Mahanadi at Satkosia. It is an easy add-on to a Puri, Konark and Bhubaneswar trip.
quickAnswer: Odisha's main wildlife destinations are Similipal Tiger Reserve, known for sal forest, waterfalls and melanistic tigers; Bhitarkanika National Park, with India's largest population of saltwater crocodiles; Chilika lake for Irrawaddy dolphins at Satapada and winter birds at Mangalajodi; and Satkosia on the Mahanadi. Similipal usually opens in November and closes in the monsoon; Bhitarkanika closes from May to July for crocodile nesting.
takeaways: Similipal was one of India's first nine tiger reserves and has rare melanistic tigers.
Bhitarkanika has India's largest population of saltwater crocodiles.
Bhitarkanika closes from 1 May to 31 July for crocodile breeding.
Chilika has Irrawaddy dolphins at Satapada and huge flocks of winter birds.
Olive ridley turtles nest in mass at Gahirmatha and Rushikulya in late winter.

items.name: Similipal
body: A large plateau of sal forest with the Barehipani and Joranda waterfalls, elephants, gaur and tigers, including rare melanistic individuals.

items.name: Bhitarkanika
body: Boat trips through mangrove creeks from Khola and Dangmal to see saltwater crocodiles, monitor lizards, deer and kingfishers.

items.name: Chilika and Mangalajodi
body: Boats from Satapada to look for Irrawaddy dolphins near the sea mouth, and community-run boats at Mangalajodi for close views of waterbirds.

items.name: Satkosia
body: A gorge on the Mahanadi with gharials, muggers and a quiet forest, with river camps.

sections.heading: Olive ridley turtles
paras: Olive ridleys come ashore together in mass nesting events, called arribadas, at Gahirmatha, Rushikulya and Devi river mouth, usually between about February and April. Hatchlings emerge around 45 to 60 days later. Visits at Rushikulya are organised with the forest department and local volunteers; watch from a distance and never use lights on the beach at night.

sections.heading: Tips
list: Visit Mangalajodi at sunrise, when birds are most active and the light is best.
Choose Satapada boat operators who keep their distance from dolphins and switch off engines.
Check Similipal's opening dates each season; they can shift with weather.

sections.heading: Where to stay and how long
paras: Similipal has forest department nature camps inside and hotels in Baripada. Bhitarkanika has forest lodges at Dangmal and hotels at Chandbali. For Chilika, stay at Satapada, Barkul or Mangalajodi's eco-cottages, or visit from Puri. Two nights each for Similipal and Bhitarkanika, and a day for Chilika, make a good week.

safety: Sightings are never guaranteed; plan several drives and enjoy the landscape itself.
Stay in the vehicle or boat and follow your guide.
Book permits only through official forest department portals or trusted operators.
Never feed animals or leave litter in a park.
Crocodiles live in Bhitarkanika's creeks; never put hands in the water.
packing: Hat, sunscreen and water for boats

faqs.q: Which is the best wildlife sanctuary in Odisha?
faqs.a: Similipal for forest and tigers, Bhitarkanika for crocodiles and Chilika for dolphins and birds.
From 1 May to 31 July for crocodile breeding.

faqs.q: Where can I see dolphins in Odisha?
faqs.a: Irrawaddy dolphins at Chilika, on boats from Satapada.

faqs.q: When do olive ridleys nest in Odisha?
faqs.a: Mass nesting usually happens between about February and April.

faqs.q: Can I combine wildlife with Puri and Konark?
faqs.a: Yes. Chilika is about an hour or so from Puri, and Bhitarkanika about four hours from Bhubaneswar.
Yes, including rare melanistic tigers, though sightings are uncommon in its dense forest.
Usually around 1 November, closing in the monsoon; check the forest department's dates.
